 SpaceX launch could create ‘space jellyfish’ over Central Florida skies
 Hour-long window opens at 6:30 a.m. Tuesday
 Chris Raines , Producer
 Published:  October 19, 2026 at 8:16 AM Updated:  October 19, 2026 at 7:23 PM Tags:  Space , SpaceX , Brevard County , Cape Canaveral BREVARD COUNTY, Fla. – Looking to the sky over Central Florida on Tuesday morning, you’ll have a chance to see a rocket heading to orbit from Cape Canaveral, and potentially a beautiful sight. 
 SpaceX is targeting a 1-hour window that opens at 6:30 a.m. Tuesday to launch the Bandwagon-5 mission aboard a Falcon 9 rocket. The mission was originally supposed to launch Monday morning, but was scrubbed due to unfavorable recovery weather conditions. 
 The mission is carrying a number of smaller satellites and re-entry vehicles into orbit for a rideshare mission. The re-entry vehicles will eventually be used to carry some, if not all, of those satellites back to Earth. 
 But the coolest part of this mission may happen as the rocket heads into space, where we could see a ‘space jellyfish’ like the one we saw about a week ago. 
 A ‘space jellyfish’ happens when the sun is shining on the upper atmosphere, though it is still dark outside. When the rocket exhaust reaches those high altitudes, the gases expand and are illuminated by the sunlight, creating a glowing, bulb-shaped cloud with wispy trails that resemble tentacles. From below, the effect can look almost otherworldly.
 We got to see some spectacular pictures of this last week.

 The launch is the 19th flight for the first stage booster, which also launched SpaceX and NASA’s Crew-9 mission, along with 10 Starlink missions and countless others.
 Following stage separation, the first stage will attempt to land on the A Shortfall of Gravitas droneship, which will be stationed in the Atlantic Ocean.
 A backup opportunity is available Wednesday if the mission doesn’t launch.
